# NPM Improved v1.6.9 — Recovery from orphaned Nginx proxy hosts

## Fix: no more ghost proxy hosts after failed SSL creation
- Fix failed proxy-host creation rollback to remove a previously generated Nginx config before deleting the uncommitted database record.
- If the Nginx removal or reload cannot complete, keep the database record visible for safe recovery instead of leaving an undetectable active configuration.
- Detect orphaned generated Nginx `.conf` files on backend startup by comparing proxy-host, redirection-host, and dead-host directories to enabled, non-deleted database records.
- Quarantine any verified orphan in a dedicated backup directory outside Nginx's active includes; validate and reload Nginx, restoring the original configuration if validation or reload fails.
- Never infer orphan status if the database is unavailable; recheck records before moving files; skip symlinks, custom files, and nonnumeric filenames.
- Reconcile orphan files before refreshing live hosts to current ACME challenge templates.

## Verification
- Backend tests and repository health passed.
- Production Docker and native updater integration tests passed.
- Actual two-node NPMX HTTP-01 challenge relay passed.
- New end-to-end regression test reproduces an orphan virtual host swallowing a challenge, quarantines the orphan, and confirms the same HTTP-01 path recovers.
- SQLite ↔ MariaDB database migration integration and required checks passed.

## Deployment
- Update the NPMX primary first, then secondaries.
- No additional containers or external certificate services are required.
- Existing custom proxy-host access lists such as GG Private are retained.
- A live certificate issuance request is separate from this automated cleanup enhancement.
